subject: Post-demo: APAC failover, latency & routing clarifications
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connell <liam.o@vertexfin.com>, Emma Stone <emma.stone@vertexfin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: APAC failover, latency & routing clarifications

Hi Liam / Emma — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a set of clarifying questions so we can scope the performance work and draft the Mutual Action Plan.

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Primary product: customer support chat + automated summarization across accounts.
- Peak traffic expectation: heavy batch during EOD reconciliation windows (EU evening / US afternoon) and sustained chat traffic globally.
- Hard constraint: EU-regulated PII (payment identifiers, KYC snippets) must remain in EU at rest.
- Desired behavior: primary routing to regional clusters with APAC as failover for US/EU in DR scenarios.

Open questions we need from you (short answers ok):
1) Latency targets: can you confirm p95 and p99 targets by region? From the demo you hinted at p95 <= 200ms for chat in US/EU; do you expect the same for APAC or relaxed (e.g., p95 <= 300ms)?
2) Concurrency and throughput: what peak concurrent requests (streams + non-streamed gen) should we size for? are there burst windows (seconds-level spikes)?
3) Streaming requirements: do you need chunked streaming (SSE/HTTP chunked) for partial message delivery? If so, what's the average token rate per stream and acceptable stream duration?
4) Residency nuance: EU data must be stored in EU — is logging/audit evidence required to be stored in-region as well, or is aggregated telemetry allowed to cross regions?
5) Failover policy: should APAC be used only for read/failover or also as an active region for serving traffic for APAC customers?

Next steps proposed from Redwood:
- We’ll produce a short SLO proposal (p95/p99 by region + concurrency headroom) and a 48-hour perf-run plan for the most common prompt shapes you sent.
- If you confirm dedicated EU residency for regulated accounts, we’ll size Dedicated pools in eu-west and propose autoscale/burst settings for APAC failover.

Can you reply with quick bullets for Q1–Q5 above by EOD tomorrow? I’ll loop in Vivek (infra) once we have numbers so he can confirm capacity.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment stubs: SLO-cheatsheet.pdf (summary), redwood-dedicated-arch.drawio (arch sketch)

From: Liam O'Connell <liam.o@vertexfin.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Stone <emma.stone@vertexfin.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: APAC failover, latency & routing clarifications

Hi Neha — great recap. Answers below (short bullets as requested):

1) Latency targets:
- US: p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 400ms for chat turns.
- EU: p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 450ms.
- APAC: acceptable to be relaxed — p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 600ms.

2) Concurrency / throughput:
- Peak concurrent streams: ~1,200 globally (mostly US/EU), expected steady-state concurrent ~300.
- Peak non-streamed gen (batch endpoints): ~300 QPS during EOD windows; bursts can spike 2x for ~60s.

3) Streaming: yes — chunked streaming (SSE or HTTP/2 chunked) is required for the chat UI. Typical token rate per stream ~8–14 tokens/sec; median session duration ~45s, heavy sessions up to 5m.

4) Residency: EU regulated PII must be persisted in-region. Audit logs that contain raw PII must also be stored in EU. Aggregated telemetry (metrics, call counts, anonymized latency histograms) can be centralized in US for ops.

5) Failover policy: prefer active regional routing — APAC can be active for APAC customers. For EU regulated accounts, APAC or US must not serve their persisted PII; only read-only replication (if any) should be permitted outside EU and must be tokenized/hashed.

Let us know if you want us to prioritize APAC routing tests; we can carve out a small test cohort next month.

— Liam
Liam O'Connell
Head of Platform Engineering | Vertex Financial
liam.o@vertexfin.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo: APAC failover, latency & routing clarifications

Following Liam's answers — quick internal notes and ask: 

- Good that streaming is required; streaming changes cost model and per-connection capacity. We should propose a hybrid config: Dedicated EU pods for regulated accounts + Hosted US for scale + edge routing in APAC (managed pools).
- Proposed SLO draft (for discussion with infra):
  * US p95 180ms / p99 400ms
  * EU p95 200ms / p99 450ms (with in-region persistence for PII)
  * APAC p95 300ms / p99 600ms (edge routing + burst protection)
- Throughput sizing notes we need from infra: what’s required to sustain 1,200 concurrent SSE streams with median token rate 10 t/s and headroom for 2x burst for 60s.

Action items:
1) Neha — confirm if Vertex wants a Dedicated EU deployment (they indicated yes) so we can propose cost + lead time.
2) Marissa / Vivek — can you draft a 48–72 hour perf plan scoped to the chat prompt shapes? Include streaming stress harness. Link to perf-run plan once ready.

I’ll also capture this in the deal record (HubSpot) and flag for sales-engine review on pricing for streaming.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: APAC failover, latency & routing clarifications — infra checklist + attachments

Thanks — I reviewed Vertex's numbers and sketched a practical checklist: 

1) Residency & data flow- We can support Dedicated EU for persistence of regulated PII. Audit logs that contain raw PII will be retained in-region for the regulated accounts. Aggregated telemetry will be forwarded to central telemetry pipelines (US) with PII redaction.

2) Latency feasibility- US/EU targets (p95 180–200ms) are feasible on Dedicated pools with the following caveats: sequence length and model size matter. For base LLM (up to 8k context) we can meet p95 targets with 16–32 token generation averages. APAC p95 at 300ms is achievable if traffic is routed to APAC edge pools and we accept lower capacity headroom or provision extra nodes for burst windows.

3) Concurrency & streaming- To sustain ~1,200 concurrent SSE streams at 10 t/s median, estimate required GPU pools: 8 dedicated A100-class instances with continuous batching + accelerated tokenizer instances for front-end fanout. If Vertex wants guaranteed headroom (1.5x), plan for 12 instances. Exact sizing depends on model choice and quantization.

4) Perf-run plan (attached)
- I attached perf-run-plan.docx and a short SLO reference (SLO-cheatsheet.pdf). Proposed run window: 48 hours with staged ramps: 0.5x, 1x, 2x bursts. Include a test cohort in APAC with active routing and EU-regulated accounts pinned to EU pods.

5) Next steps for timeline/cost- If Vertex signs for Dedicated EU now, procurement lead time ~4–6 weeks for reserved capacity; initial perf run can be scheduled within 10 business days if we get scope.

Action items (owners):
- Neha: confirm Dedicated EU and whether Vertex will sign an NDA + SOC 2 access for audit evidence.
- Ben/Marissa: finalize perf-run test plan and share link (Marissa will own orchestration).
- Infra (me): run an initial capacity calc and attach a compact cost delta for 8 vs 12 instance options.

I’ll upload the artifacts to the deal folder and share a short checklist: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/0B_perf_run_plan

— Vivek
